tasks.gr12-paper1-human-reproduction-homeostas: Topic: Paper 1 Consolidation — Human Reproduction and Homeostasis. Revise the reproductive systems, menstrual cycle, fertilisation, implantation, pregnancy, the placenta, hormonal control, blood glucose regulation and thermoregulation. Ask Grade 12 learners to answer exam-style application questions that integrate these systems.
tasks.gr12-paper1-response-coordination-plants: Topic: Paper 1 Consolidation — Response Coordination and Plant Responses. Revise the nervous system, reflex arcs, receptors, the eye, the ear, endocrine glands, negative feedback, homeostasis, plant hormones and tropisms. Ask Grade 12 learners to interpret diagrams and explain coordinated responses in humans and plants.
tasks.gr12-paper2-genetics-evolution-consolida: Topic: Paper 2 Consolidation. Revise DNA, protein synthesis, meiosis, genetics, pedigrees, sex linkage, evolution by natural selection and human evolution. Ask Grade 12 learners to answer integrated Paper 2 questions, including genetic crosses, evidence-based evolution items and structured explanatory responses.
tasks.gr12-cradle-of-humankind-t4: Topic: The Cradle of Humankind (Grade 12, Term 4, Human Evolution continued). Cover the Cradle of Humankind as a World Heritage Site in Gauteng and North West with limestone caves that preserve hominin fossils; the main sites and what they gave: Taung (Taung Child, Australopithecus africanus, Raymond Dart, 1924), Sterkfontein (Mrs Ples, Robert Broom; Little Foot, Ron Clarke; Phillip Tobias), Kromdraai (Paranthropus robustus, Broom), Swartkrans (C.K. Brain), Malapa (Australopithecus sediba, Lee Berger); later sites Florisbad, Border Cave and Blombos Cave (early modern humans, symbolic thinking); evolutionary trends from Australopithecus to Homo (bigger brain, bipedalism shown by a short wide pelvis and S-shaped spine, smaller teeth and jaws, flatter face); dating of fossils (carbon-14 only for young fossils, other radioactive isotopes in the rock for older ones). Give ages only as approximate ('about'). Ask Grade 12 learners to match sites, fossils and scientists and to describe trends.
tasks.gr12-alternatives-to-evolution-t4: Topic: Alternatives to Evolution (Grade 12, Term 4). Cover cultural and religious explanations of the origin and development of life as views people hold, kept separate from the scientific theory of evolution by natural selection (evidence that can be tested): Creationism (life was created by a creator such as God), Intelligent Design (complex features of life point to an intelligent designer), Literalism (a holy text such as the Genesis story read as an exact account of events), Theistic evolution (God used evolution; accepts the evidence for evolution), and a traditional creation story as a cultural example. Test only what each term MEANS and how they differ; never ask which explanation is right or wrong, and never rank beliefs. Ask Grade 12 learners to define, identify and compare.
